General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Purexbox ↗ Open Full Page

Review: GTA 6 (Xbox) - The Most Breathtaking Open-World Game Of All Time

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1570 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Purexbox

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Where do you even start with a game like GTA 6?
  • We've all spent the last 13 years trying to figure out what GTA 6 might look like by the time it arrives, and the answer is perhaps more simplistic than some had theorised - it's basically GTA 5 mixed with Red Dead Redemption 2, but with a ton of added detail and ambition on top.
  • It has been revealed that before we get to the open world, which is surely the most incredible aspect of the entire game, we should first touch on the story of Lucia and Jason.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Where do you even start with a game like GTA 6? Not only is it the most highly-anticipated video game we've ever seen, but it's also attempting to live up to ridiculous expectations set by its predecessors over the years. GTA 3 revolutionised how we thought about 3D open-world epics, Vice City and San Andreas pushed things to the next level, GTA 4 took yet another massive step into the HD era, and GTA 5 propelled the series into another stratosphere.

We've all spent the last 13 years trying to figure out what GTA 6 might look like by the time it arrives, and the answer is perhaps more simplistic than some had theorised - it's basically GTA 5 mixed with Red Dead Redemption 2, but with a ton of added detail and ambition on top. That's all it needed to be, and I reckon people are going to absolutely love it.

It has been revealed that before we get to the open world, which is surely the most incredible aspect of the entire game, we should first touch on the story of Lucia and Jason. These two amateur criminals accidentally run into each other and establish a relationship (which can alter between platonic and romantic depending on how you interact throughout the campaign), and after a simple score goes wrong, they find themselves being dragged into more and more dangerous scenarios. That's the basic premise, and the rest is up for you to discover yourself.

Industry observers note that the GTA 6 Extended Preview from a few months ago left me very concerned about whether there was enough intrigue to the two main characters (along with the NPCs for that matter), but I needn't have worried. Lucia is a fiesty, hot-headed personality - the type of person who thinks less about the consequences and more about the high life she's determined to acquire - while Jason is extremely laid back to a hilarious extent at times, although also highly capable in pretty much any situation he finds himself in. The two bounce off each other really nicely, and their dynamic definitely remains engaging throughout the campaign's duration.

According to recent reports, while I really don't want to spoil anything story-related, the mission structure is very much what you'd expect from GTA 5 and RDR2. In other words, there's a well-balanced mix of laid-back and humorous missions along with more intense shootouts and getaways that significantly ramp up in intensity. They've managed to get really inventive and ambitious with some of the later missions in particular, and I think there's no doubt they're the best of any GTA game.

Sources indicate that I also want to point out the use of music in GTA 6's missions, which caught me off-guard and became one of my low-key favourite features. In a nutshell, if you find yourself in the likes of a shootout or a getaway, you'll often notice that curated tunes play in the background to amplify the situation. The developers sometimes even go a step further by making the lighting around you pulsate to the beat, or by introducing lyricists to create a menacing vibe, and it can turn an otherwise generic mission into an amazing one. Seriously, I can't overstate how much I love this feature.

The story itself takes 40ish hours if you completely rush it (which admittedly I've been doing for the most part to hit this embargo), but if you take your time and do at least a decent amount of the optional stuff, it's likely more around 60-100+ hours. As I say, I've enjoyed all of those hours, and I think the campaign seriously hits its stride in the final third - the vast majority of memorable moments are saved for the latter stages.

Industry observers note that I don't want you to fixate on the 40-100+ hour figure though, and that's because GTA 6's open world is so incredible and so vast that you could be playing it for months, and likely years, and not see everything it has to offer. We've never seen a GTA world like this - traffic levels are extremely high, the number of NPCs on the streets is ridiculous, it always feels like something's happening around every corner (there are so many random encounters!), you'll find loads of buildings you can go into, there's so much detail on everything... it's just an absolute dream for anyone who loves the idea of immersing themselves in this game.

GTA 5 had an amazing open world too, but after going back and playing it for the purpose of this review, there are two major differences that stand out - there's far less actually happening in the world at any one time (and therefore much less to interact with), and the map just feels tiny in comparison. GTA 6's state of Leonida incorporates so much more than just Vice City itself, including many other highly-populated areas such as Key Lento and Ambrosia. The first time you actually see Vice City in a mission (assuming you haven't gone and explored it previously) is a highlight of the entire game - it immediately appears so vast and so incredibly detailed that it feels like a next-gen experience.

The way in which you interact with that world as a player has evolved as well. Cops are smarter than ever, and not only prove a tough challenge when attempting a getaway at three stars or more, but they also remember what you look like - and therefore you sometimes have to disguise yourself by changing into different outfits. Stealing a car now requires you to think about what kind of lock system it has on it, and whether there's a tracker fitted that will alert the police to your location. Cars can even run out of fuel now! Every element feels more in-depth than we've seen in GTA in the past, but Rockstar has crucially balanced the impact just right, so it's never to the detriment of your ability to just have fun.

I do think you'll get the most out of the game if you pace yourself though. It feels intentionally designed to encourage a slow playstyle where you explore, hang out, browse the fully-featured social media and news feeds on your phone (complete with video clips and comment sections), take part in games like pool and minigolf, engage in countless side-missions and random encounters, watch and play a ridiculous amount of purpose-built content on your in-game TV, and ultimately just see what you can discover without rapidly jumping from mission-to-mission. The amount of content here is overwhelming, but in a really satisfying way.

Of course, it's almost a given at this point that GTA 6 looks visually incredible, and I can confirm that it's definitely a stunner on Xbox Series X. There's some occasional pop-in, but it's minimal, and I only ran into a few tiny bugs during the review period (which may have been ironed out for release anyway). The performance is mostly very smooth considering the circumstances as well - yes, it's a bit jarring at first to go back to 30FPS if you've been playing 60FPS games for the most part in recent years, but give it an hour-or-two, and you probably won't care anymore. Seriously, it's a total non-issue for me at this point, and I'm more than happy playing at 30FPS.

It should be noted that I played around 30 hours on a VRR-enabled display during the review period, and around 10 hours without one. I was perfectly happy with the performance in both cases, with the only noticeably big frame rate drops occurring during very rare and visually intensive gameplay sequences.

According to recent reports, so, is there anything I don't like about GTA 6? The only thing I'd say is that it doesn't top my tier list in terms of greatest GTA stories ever, although it's probably still in the top three. It's a narrative that'll fully invest most players from start to finish, and there are shocking moments and twists that are bound to last long in the memory, but I also reckon it gets a bit too convoluted and farcical at times. That noted, the final third of the campaign is jam-packed with intense story elements and incredibly action-packed missions, guaranteeing some truly jaw-dropping moments.

According to recent reports, its tone can also feel overly harsh and uncomfortably serious in specific circumstances, but hey... this is Grand Theft Auto after all. Every GTA has its moments like that, but the impact feels more striking this time due to the enhanced sense of realism. Fortunately, there's plenty of lighthearted humour to be found along the way as well.

Somehow, GTA 6 lives up to the hype. Rockstar Games has crafted the most incredible open world I've ever experienced in a video game, packed with so much detail that I'll want to continue exploring it for months and likely years to come. It's coupled with a campaign that's full of extremely entertaining missions, led by two main characters who I've become much more invested in than I'd anticipated.

I'd have been fuming if you'd told me in 2013 that I'd have to wait 13 more years for the next GTA game, but now that it's finally here, I'm just relieved they've somehow managed to pull off another Game of the Decade contender once again.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that there are plenty of controversial game franchises out there. But many are pretty lazy, and either intentionally racist, sexist or simply provocative. A truly controversial series is one that sets out to do something, and does so in an unapologetic and probably disturbing way. In unrelated news, Running With Scissors' Postal Classic & Uncut is out now on Google Play!

Unlike, say, Postal II, there's no wackiness or crass humour here. The story is simple: You are the Dude, and everybody else has to die. That means blasting your way through dozens of levels ranging from suburban neighbourhoods to downtown metropolises, with a variety of firearms and explosives, as you face down police officers, armed residents and plenty of unarmed civilians caught in the crossfire.

Recent findings suggest that the Earth is Hungry Postal is a series that, while I won't necessarily defend, I think everyone will agree has an undercurrent of potential. The original Postal veers between exciting and chilling, as each level is interspersed with the paranoid ramblings of the Dude. And while the official story may be that you're defending yourself against crazed gunmen, all those people running for their lives may beg to differ.

Industry observers note that in other words, you're stepping into the disturbed mind of a crazed gunman. Not hard to see why this was so controversial back in the day.

Sources indicate that it's a thoroughly dark, brooding and unnerving concept, and one that Running With Scissors are revisiting in the upcoming Flesh & Wire, a more horror-focused FPS set in the aftermath of the Dude's rampage. Of course, if you strip all that away, Postal remains a pretty solid isometric shooter and a real 90s snapshot.

If you've got a strong stomach for it, you can find Postal Classic & Uncut available on Android, with all 16 original levels and four from the Special Delivery expansion included.

Recent findings suggest that postal Classic & Uncut is definitely not a cheery game for the weekend. So if you need something a little calmer and more laid-back, why not check out our latest list of the five newly introduced mobile games to try this week?

After weeks of waiting, Arc Raiders developer Embark has officially unveiled the first few months of the game’s 2026 roadmap. The blueprint is split into four months, covering January to April, collectively dubbed Escalation.

We’re expecting a content patch each month, with the majority of the biggest additions happening on the game’s existing maps. There is, however, at least one newly introduced map in the works, but it won’t be here until sometime in April.

In a recent development, while we wait for that, Arc Raiders is going to go through several events and other in-game changes, some more meaningful (and exciting) than others. January looks to be the lightest so far, which makes sense given that it’s just a week or so from ending.

January’s chapter is titled Headwinds, kicking off on January 27. This segment will see the addition of a new matchmaking option for players above level 40 - at or near the game’s endgame. We’re also expecting a new Map Condition, and a new Player Project for everyone to contribute to.

Industry observers note that things start getting interesting in February, when Shrouded Sky will begin. This chapter brings three exciting additions to Arc Raiders. There will be a fresh Map Condition, new Arc Threat, and the start of another Player Project.

Interestingly, we’re going to see some sort of map upgrade during the month, but Embark didn’t share anymore details. The next Raider Deck will also deploy in February, alongside a latest Expedition Window.

The Flashpoint chapter begins in March, when we’re expecting another newly introduced Map Condition, one more new Arc Threat, as well as another Player Project. March’s most interesting addition is an update to everyone’s trusty rooster friend, Scrappy.

Finally, April is when the major guns come out, because that’s when the first newly introduced map of 2026 will arrive in Arc Raiders. With it, comes a new large Arc, which is to be expected. A new Map Condition will debut then, too, likely starting off on the new map.

That’s pretty much it, but seeing as we’re just one day away from the start of the January stage, things are about to get exciting again in Arc Raiders.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, mega Man: Dual Override’s 2025 reveal brought back the classic boss design contest, asking fans to create and submit their own robot masters, with Capcom choosing one to include in the game. After thousands of submissions, we have our winner; meet Cleanser Man.

It has been revealed that as his name suggests, Cleanser Man is a cleaning robot who attacks (and tidies) using a long, multi-cleaning hose arm. Capcom has provided the following character summary:.

Cleanser Man is a cleaning robot with an obsession for pristine beauty. Fueled by an extremely sensitive dirt sensor, Cleaner Man’s ideal world is one without a speck of dust. However, his devotion to cleanliness has a cost. His aggressive scrubbing causes great damage to global landmarks and historic works of art. This fixation has caused the public to view him as more of a threat than a helping hand. Furious and feeling misunderstood, Cleanser Man seizes control of trash processing facility and uses it to pollute the environment with hopes of forcing the world to appreciate the importance of cleanliness.

It has been revealed that cleanser Man won out among the six finalists, a few of which were also cleaning-themed bosses. “In the end, we chose Cleanser Man because of the unique way the concept was brought together and the originality of the color design,” says game director Shinya Ikuta. “While staying true to and respecting the original submission, we adjusted certain details to better fit the world and style of the game.”  Unfortunately, Capcom has not revealed Cleanser Man's creator, but you can see the character in action in the reveal video below.

In addition to Cleanser Man, Mega Man: Dual Override's rogues' gallery includes the following revealed robot masters: Twinkle Girl, Jet Man, Tank Man, and Cook Man. The remaining three bosses have yet to be revealed.

Industry observers note that mega Man: Dual Override launches in 2027 for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, Switch, and PC. To learn more about the game, read our extended preview here. You can also check out the game's recently revealed amiibo figures for the Switch versions.

If you couldn’t guess already, the fresh theme is Bloom Festival, inspired by Chinese New Year celebrations.

In a recent development, the significant upcoming story chapter takes place in the Infinity Nikki’s Wanxiang Realm. This deceptively serene and blissful region hides a dark secret, however. Chromafaces, the mythical inhabitants of the realm, have to embody fixed identities that dictate how they live and work.

Sources indicate that these are doled out through Character Tokens, which are used to assign roles to each individual. The story follows Nikki as she uncovers the script that runs the realm and the facade it props up. Nikki will help free Chromafaces and dispel the illusion.

Recent findings suggest that the Wanxiang Realm is split into three areas. Cai Ye is your typical lantern-lit district, where festivals and fireworks happen. Kongming Gorge is almost the opposite of that; a quiet and cold place. Finally, Jiuhua Pavilion literally floats above the region, and it's home to neverending music and dance.

According to recent reports, the other significant addition in 2.2 are the two fresh 5-Star Resonance Outfits with some interesting gameplay implications. Where Wanxiang Weaves Life is inspired by wuxia aesthetics, and true to its inspirations, it lets Nikki shapeshift into different Spirit Personas - and automatically collect resources in her vicinity.

It has been revealed that chroma's Mortal Heart, on the other hand, allows Nikki to fly around the Wanxiang Realm, drawing on the power of the Celestial Deer. This outfit also uses Celestial Deer Vision to automatically ping and mark treasure chests around her.

You can also look forward to Nefarious Shadows, a newly introduced Ability Outfit, which lets Nikki see through disguises, and reveals hidden paths in the world.

It has been revealed that as with every major upgrade, of course, there are themed activities and limited-time events throughout. Hotpot House is a cooking minigame where you attempt to run the eponymous restaurant, whereas Flavor Frenzy is series of platforming challenges that tasks you with gathering ingredients. Fortune Mahjong is a little more straightforward, with support for solo and multiplayer play.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Since 2023, the Recording Academy has included an official category for video game soundtracks, adding an air of legitimacy to a diverse musical medium we know and love.
  • As is often the case, what stands out most about these nominees is how, generally speaking, they don't fully align with gaming culture's favorite soundtracks of the year, and instead often trend toward the most recognizable IP (often franchises with films) of the year.
  • The standout here is Ghost of Yōtei, which is not an adaptation of the massive franchises the other games fall into.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since 2023, the Recording Academy has included an official category for video game soundtracks, adding an air of legitimacy to a diverse musical medium we know and love. Today, we learned the list of nominees for the 2027 Grammy ceremony, and it's an interesting lineup. The nominations are as follows:.

As is often the case, what stands out most about these nominees is how, generally speaking, they don't fully align with gaming culture's favorite soundtracks of the year, and instead often trend toward the most recognizable IP (often franchises with films) of the year. On that note, it's most surprising to see that Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora has been nominated for the third year in a row: once for the base game, once for the Secrets of the Spires DLC, and now for the From The Ashes DLC. None of these soundtracks are bad by any means, but their Grammy representation far outweighs their cultural footprint.

The standout here is Ghost of Yōtei, which is not an adaptation of the massive franchises the other games fall into. However, it's also a Sony-published game, which have a pretty good track record of getting nominations, potentially due to the company's massive presence in the music and film industries. Still, Ghost of Yōtei has a great, unique score that's deserving of its spot, and also one previously nominated for best music at the 2025 Game Awards. The Grammys accept any releases between October 1 of one year and September 30 of the following year, so Ghost of Yōtei barely made the cut for this window. The Game Awards nominees will be confirmed tomorrow – it will be interesting to see how much overlap there is between the categories.

This batch of Grammy noms also has fewer recurring nominees than past years. This is Gordy Haab's third nomination (he won in 2024 for Star Wars Jedi: Survivor) and John Paesano's second nomination (he was nominated in 2025 for Marvel's Spider-Man 2). It's also the first year since the awards' creation without Bear McCreary or Austin Wintory nominations.

Last year's nominations left a sour taste in the mouths of many, with several DLC nominees and a complete lack of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, the year's standout hit that many specifically praised for its music. This year certainly has snubs (Mewgenics, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, and Control Resonant all come to mind), but none as egregious as last year.

What do you think was the best video game score from the last year? Let us know in the comments!

But in Cell to Singularity, developer Computer Lunch has been working towards a simulation of everything, with the latest major step being their Future patch.

Cell to Singularity is, essentially, exactly what it says on the tin. Your goal is to explore and guide a simulation of an entire human civilisation, starting from simple single-celled organisms all the way up to the space-faring apes we all know and love. And the Future expansion, naturally, takes you into the speculative future of space travel and beyond.

In a recent development, that includes elements ranging from space tourism to artificial general intelligence and beyond. All of which it's up to you to guide in different directions, seeing humanity change and grow as they go beyond orbit and away to the moon and beyond, establishing a permanent presence away from the planet.

You'll have access to the newly introduced Prediction Matrix to boost your progress, as well as a revamped Mission System and more. All this, and more music too! The Future, it seems, has never looked brighter for fans of Cell to Singularity.

Recent findings suggest that but what about everyone else? GTA 6 is nominated for Game of the Year at The Game Awards, so does it live up to that recommendation? Are the critics overwhelmingly enamoured with it? That's what we've been intrigued to find out.

So, here's what the critics are saying about GTA 6 so far:.

It has been revealed that "A game so good I asked our tech team if I could somehow give it 11/10. GTA 6 is an absolute masterclass in genre-mashing. Given the state of the industry, it's sobering that we might never see another game like this again. Grand Theft Auto 6 is a cover-to-cover masterpiece without equal.".

"Grand Theft Auto VI is a generational game that stands toe-to-toe with many of the great crime stories and satires across other media. It showcases both the entertainment value of interactive play and the current high-water mark for technical and artistic detail in games. Hunt for and count up all the minor faults or foibles you like, but then note how you just spent another hour lost in this remarkable escape into criminality, wanton violence, egregious sex, and the elusive potential of true love.".

Recent findings suggest that "This game is the culmination of everything the developer has previously achieved in the open-world space that pushes the genre to heights that, in all likelihood, no other developer will be able to reach. GTA 6 is an astonishing open-world action game that I’d wager won’t be outdone until Grand Theft Auto 7.".

In a recent development, "GTA 6 is the highest-fidelity sandbox of its generation. Rockstar has built an open world of truly astonishing scale, scope, and quality. There's a degree of sophistication to everything GTA 6 does, and there's no aspect of the series' gameplay that hasn't been improved over past instalments.".

Recent findings suggest that "I regularly find myself in love with video games, but it’s extraordinarily rare that I find myself in complete awe of them. Put simply, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the single most impressive video game I have ever played.".

Recent findings suggest that "A game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale, Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that.".

Sources indicate that "Grand Theft Auto VI delivers a remarkably immersive and ambitious open-world experience, blending thrilling gameplay, diverse activities, and a compelling relationship between Jason and Lucia. While uneven storytelling, pacing problems, and occasional performance drops prevent it from reaching perfection, the richly realized world of Leonida and its extraordinary attention to detail make this an unforgettable crime adventure that largely lives up to its monumental expectations.".

Industry observers note that "Grand Theft Auto VI is a great game that lives up to so much of the hype and expectations. You do have so much more freedom with how to tackle missions, though, and Leonida is a world filled with things to do and discover that will keep you coming back for a long time.".

In a recent development, history tells us that we should have always expected a mainline Grand Theft Auto game to get incredible review scores, but it was really hard to see how they'd live up to expectations with this one. Nevertheless, they've somehow done it!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After an incredibly long wait, Grand Theft Auto 6 has dropped to massively positive reviews from critics, who have repeatedly described Rockstar's latest release as one of, if not the best games ever made. While there was plenty of debate over whether the critic reviews and player responses would actually line up or not when it released, the public response has been almost equally impressive so far.

Despite taking the industry by storm and boasting sales that broke a upcoming record for the entertainment industry, GTA 6's review rating has just plummeted on Metacritic immediately after the site opened its user scores.

As noted by consumers like CharlieIntel on X, while there are plenty of user reviews that note the flaws while celebrating its achievements, the User Review section for GTA 6 on Metacritic has been absolutely flooded with overwhelmingly negative reviews, many of which are from players who admit they "haven't even played the game" themselves.

With GTA 6 at the moment sitting at a 5.1 user score at the time of writing, over half of the reviews uploaded for the game are negative, with countless politically charged reviews calling it "woke slop" and a "cuck simulator" over its relationship gameplay mechanics, or consumers straight-up keyboard-smashing negative reviews just so they can contribute to tearing down the game's score.

While it isn't exactly surprising that one of the most widely talked about games in history would wind up being the target of annoyed players or internet trolls wanting to join in on the fun, Take-Two had already expressed their concern about this exact situation happening years before GTA 6 released.

Even Nintendo's recently released Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake wasn't exempt from the same fate either, with Link's return being slammed by players in response to the game's popularity, rather than the actual quality of the remake.

Considering that there are some genuine complaints to be had surrounding GTA 6's console performance, control scheme, or returning franchise features that are currently absent in the newest release, it's hard to pinpoint what the actual score will end up being after the dust of its release settles.

If the critic scores and the Metacritic rating for Rockstar's previous games are anything to go by, however, Grand Theft Auto 6 will likely wind up with an incredibly high score regardless of the current review bomb storm, especially as the game gets even bigger with the eventual PC port and multiplayer release.

#52126. GTA 6: Best Starter Car to Register

GTA 6: Best Starter Car to Register

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (626 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • During your Grand Theft Auto 6 playthrough, you will eventually get the opportunity to register a car.
  • According to recent reports, this opportunity comes at the start of Chapter 2, where you learn about a man named Moses who deals with stolen cars.
  • Instead of stealing the coolest car to register, I recommend going a different route.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

During your Grand Theft Auto 6 playthrough, you will eventually get the opportunity to register a car. Registering cars allows you to call them easily from your phone with a small BuckMe fee.

According to recent reports, this opportunity comes at the start of Chapter 2, where you learn about a man named Moses who deals with stolen cars. To unlock Moses and his shop for good, you need to bring him your very first car to register.

Instead of stealing the coolest car to register, I recommend going a different route. Here’s the best starter car to register in GTA 6.

Sources indicate that during the first mission of Chapter 2 in GTA 6, you will naturally meet a girl named Vicki. During this mission, Vicki will eventually mention Moses to Lucia, and once she does, Moses shop will be marked on the map with the objective to bring him a starter car to register.

After bringing Moses one car and registering it with him for free, you will unlock the ability to register most cars in Leonida. The only cars you can’t register with Moses are the ones with trackers, so make a mental note of that.

Also, keep in mind that even though you can register your starter car for free, registering every other car from here on out will cost you money. The price of registration depends on the type of car.

Sources indicate that while players may want to steal and register the flashiest car in Leonida as their starter, this isn’t necessarily the smartest move. The nice sports cars won’t have the most trunk space and can be hard to control.

Instead, it would be best to choose a pickup truck for a starter car, as they have a ton of stash space and are generally easy to drive.

It may seem unimportant, but having more stash space will allow Lucia to transport more money and robbery loot on a single trip. This means you can gather money faster, without constantly needing to visit ATMs.

Recent findings suggest that additionally, as previously mentioned, pickup trucks are generally on the easier side to control when driving. This is important early in the game since it will allow you to have an easier time exploring, crashing less, and avoiding the need to pay for repairs.

Once you've built up wealth by using your starter car as a getaway and stash for loot from robberies and muggings, you can use any extra cash to register nicer vehicles.

Simply put, the coolest cars tend to have the highest registration price, so you want a reliable one that will help you get around easier and stash more money to start off.

It has been revealed that while there are many pickup trucks to find across the map of GTA VI, I have had the best luck finding them in parking lots. More specifically, I have found pickup trucks commonly in parking lots in front of bars, clothing shops, barbershops, etc.

In other words, pickup trucks are very easy to find, considering they aren’t that special when it comes to style and speed and aren’t considered “rare.” If you are worried about finding one in a specific color, you shouldn’t be, considering Moses makes you change the color when you bring it in.

Once you find a pickup truck (or a different car if you decided not to listen to my advice), bring it on over to Moses and tell him you’d like to register it.

After the quick transaction with Moses is complete, you are now able to call your starter car to your location whenever you like for a small BuckMe price via the Scooter Bros app on your phone.

Zenless Zone Zero’s latest Special Program has delivered a tonne of information about the game’s big upcoming patch, Version 2.6. This latest addition kicks off celebrations in Upcoming Eridu, and it’s dubbed Encore for an Old Dream.

Sources indicate that version 2.6 is not far off, either, arriving in ZZZ on February 6 - exactly one week from today. Encore for an Old Dream is something of an in-between story that takes place after the end of Season 2.

Sources indicate that the narrative of 2.6 sees the Proxies’ return to Sixth Street for Fresh Eridu's annual Gilded Carrot Day. At the centre of the celebrations is the debut of idol group Angels of Delusion at the 404 Error music venue, but not all is as it seems.

The story follows the Proxies getting invited backstage to support the group, which also includes helping them set up practice schedules, organise events and manage social media activities. There’s a rhythm minigame as part of that, along with newly introduced maps and mechanics for Marcel Adventure.

Industry observers note that angels of Delusion is also the group that the two fresh Agents being introduced in this update belong to. Members of the same group are capable of performing coordinated attacks. The new arrivals are Sunna and Aria.

According to recent reports, sunna is a an S-Rank Physical Support Agent who specialises in boosting teammates using Attack and Anomaly. Her Ultimate sees her pull out a giant hammer to land heavy damage, and bring teammates into combat using Quick Assist. Sunna’s companion, Bubblegum, can cast Cat's Gaze on enemies, marking them for detonation. Bubblegum can also buff the squad’s attack.

Sources indicate that aria is the other new arrival, the group’s lead vocalist who can shift between two forms, idol projection and construct. Aria is an Ether Anomaly Agent who also deals high burst damage, specifically against enemies who suffer from any Attribute Anomalies.

Sunna and Aria also benefit from the support of the amusingly named Bangboo Biggest Fan, a fan club president who can heal them over time, and boost the squad’s Attack any time two or more Angels of Delusion members are present.

Version 2.6’s S-Rank re-runs are Yixuan (Auric Ink - Rupture), and Yuzuha (Physical - Support), who you can look forward to as part of the banners.

Version 2.6 will also expand Hollow Zero with a new game mode, Operation Matrix. The mode offers themed stages that rotate weekly, each offering new mechanics. You can now also Sweep in Hollow Zero.

Industry observers note that beyond all the celebrations, this update also brings combat kit overhauls to a couple of older S-Rank characters, Lycaon and Harumasa. You can look forward to multiple limited-time events, too, including one where you can earn a fresh outfit for Pan Yinhu.

The significant event is naturally going to be themed around Gilded Carrot Day, and it actually starts today. There’s the usual run of login rewards (about 3,300 Polychromes), as well as daily activities. Yet another login event - Gilded Surprise, Wonderful Boo-ns - will be available February 14-23, offering daily draws from a pool of 4 billion Polychrome.

As always, there’s no reason not to catch up on the latest set of Zenless Zone Zero codes for some free in-game items.

In a recent development, in that way, I think positing it as anti gacha is a bit of a misnomer. At its core, Mixcity Swap looks to be an exciting standalone card game, and one that doesn't really need to pit itself against such a widely reviled mechanic to be successful.

It has been revealed that but, I'll certainly be interested to see how Atypique intends to grow this game in future. We've got plenty of small-scale card battlers that avoid gacha, but a long-term live-service type release may be a very different beast to keep loyal to that ideal.

According to recent reports, could Grand Theft Auto 6 come to Switch 2? That has been the substantial question ever since Nintendo officially revealed its console last year, and it's something that we have mused over ever since (as unlikely as it may seem at an initial glance). Now that the game is out, the tech experts over at Digital Foundry have weighed in on the port possibility, and, perhaps unsurprisingly, they don't rate its chances.

In the outlet's latest rundown, it touches on the "compromised" Xbox Series S performance. It isn't all that, with DF noting "frame-rates routinely lingering in the mid to high 20s during ordinary traversal and combat," but it's the system that regularly lands the most comparisons to Switch 2, so DF states that it would be "interesting" to see if it would be "possible for a further cut back version to ship on Nintendo's hybrid console".

However, the experts point out that a Switch 2 port "feels extremely unlikely at this stage".

"Unless there are massive changes made," DF's John Linneman claims around the 53:24 mark in the above video, "I don't see how this could possibly work on Switch 2".

Recent findings suggest that the main reasoning seems to mostly come down to the sheer size of the damn thing. This is a game that is pushing even the highest-end consoles to their limit — "the huge CPU burden that restricts GTA 6 to 30fps on even PS5 Pro" — so how would the comparatively little guy Switch 2 ever stand a chance?

Sources indicate that now, we're never willing to rule anything out completely. Switch 1 got its fair share of 'impossible ports' in its lifetime, and Switch 2 has already landed a handful of beefy boys that we previously never could have imagined making the jump intact. However, this one might be a step too far. Please do prove us wrong, Rockstar!

It has been revealed that it's a shame, because by all accounts, the game is fantastic. Our sister sites Push Square and Pure Xbox both gave it 10/10 reviews, praising it as one of the greatest open worlds of all time. It shot right to the top of Metacritic's ratings, too, tying with Ocarina of Time as the best of the best.

It has been revealed that hello! And welcome back to The Wrapp, where we natter about our weekend gaming prepares for a bit. This time, Catherine's taken up stamping passports as a profession while Iwan's struggling to get words down. Elsewhere, Dann and I are puzzled by the colour brown while Shaun's off being a sky pirate.

Sadly, I have been pulled back into Neopets Faerie Fragments due to them running a Neopets.com event that had a battle pass, and one way to get points in the battle pass is to play Neopets Faerie Fragments. I am happy to report that the daily runs, which challenge you to do a string of levels one after another, are far easier than where I am in the main questline! There’s also a sub-questline that doesn’t give you coins (only clothing coins?!) in a very glitched and black world, that I also was able to play through, so I have been knocking those out each day.

I’m still trying my hardest to survive Warhammer Survivors, but something else has actually caught my eye this week - and that’s Lil’ Guardsman on mobile, simply because the art style reminds me so much of Lost in Play. I’m prone to judging games by their proverbial cover, so I have a feeling I’ll enjoy this fantasy take on border patrol very, very much.

Right, time to throw these pesky humans to the dungeons (insert Lemongrab-inspired screeching here)!

Recent findings suggest that the game world is being affected this week in so many ways, some of which we have discussed, but how will it affect us? Well, multiple mobile games were released recently, and more are opting for the 'buy before you try' system. As long as they're clear about it, I think it's a pretty effective way to give folks a solid taste of something.

One such game that has been blatant about it on booting it up is Booster Pack: Heroes. I like opening cards, I like cool characters, and I like RPG elements, so this seems right up my alley… But it's only got an hour to get through it.

This month I’ve been trying my best to accomplish National Novel Writing Month. Even with the organisation being defunct, the challenge remains. But sadly, I think it’s defeated me, as 1667 words a day is surprisingly difficult if you want to, you know, have a life outside work.

In a recent development, that doesn’t mean I’m about to stop writing, though, and I’ll be working on plenty of stuff this weekend. As well as digging into an interesting newly introduced visual novel, featuring vampires, emotional therapy and some rather flashy clothes. Can’t guess what? You’ll have to wait to find out!

I’m always quite excited to see a upcoming Bart Bonte game hitting mobile. While brown certainly might not be the most appealing colour, I’m very excited to jump into his next entry in the colour series… It feels like it’s been a particularly long time since the last outing, so it’s a welcome return.

Yesterday I decided to pick up Warhammer Survivors, following the clamour from my co-workers last week. And I have to say, it is unfortunately a bit rubbish. You feel so sluggish and slow, plodding along, and if you pick a character with a Boltgun, good luck killing the weakest enemies in 3 hits. Even when you are fully decked out with the best gun and chainsword, it still feels like you are aimlessly wandering around.

In a recent development, of course, though, we can’t just ignore the big release this week. It is what we have all been waiting for; Spirit Crossing is out of Netflix exclusivity and available on iOS. I don’t know that much about it beyond it being MMO-ish, but the launch trailer shows an airship turned into a house. So, I shall be an air pirate! The closest to a modern Skies of Arcadia Legends we will apparently get.

Much like Dann, I'm happy to see Bart Bonte is back on his colours. While Leaving Home and Mister Antonio are great, they don't hit the same way Pink, Red, Orange, and so on do. They remind me of the old Flash favourite, The Impossible Quiz, which I used to love. It's like a healthy dose of nostalgia with completely fresh ideas.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that though it may seem like we just had a big life sim release in Heartopia, 2026 actually has more than one highly-anticipated release in that particular subgenre of cozy game. The next big one on the horizon is Starsand Island, the life and farming sim from Seed Sparkle Lab.

The game has been gaining momentum since the launch of a demo in October last year, but the developer never quite managed to commit to a date for its debut title. Until now.

Recent findings suggest that seed Sparkle Lab announced today that Starsand Island will enter Early Access on February 11, which is only a bit over one week from now. This goes for Steam and the Xbox Preview Program version.

Industry observers note that the developer remarked to expect a fairly short Early Access run, as the full launch is expected in the summer of this year. When the full release arrives, the game will also make the jump to PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series, as well as Switch 2.

The full release is also expected to bring Steam Deck support and introduce the multiplayer mode, which will not be available during Early Access.

Starsand Island has something of a unique look compared to other games in the subgenre. The storybook, anime-inspired aesthetics are popular in the realm of gacha games, of course. However, seeing as this particular game isn’t gacha, being a premium product means it’s going to offer something free-to-play games aren’t designed to.

Speaking of which, the game will be available in two editions: Standard and Deluxe, with the latter including Romanticism-inspired outfits, furniture, and other customisation items. If you buy either during launch, you’ll also get a Chinese New Year bonus with even more outfits and furniture.

On top of the usual systems of farming, mining, and making friends with adorable characters (and animals), the game also has combat that pits you against ancient guardians. You can, of course, also build a home in it, and decorate it to your heart's content.

Seed Sparkle Lab claims you can expect about 100 hours of content in the Early Access launch build, and more features will arrive over the course of the next six or so months, including a crossover event with My Time At Portia.

Recent findings suggest that you can look forward to more Starsand Island coverage from us in the near future. Until then, you can get started by planning who you’re going to date now.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It sounds like Koei Tecmo’s decision to finally release a Nioh game on PC day-and-date with PlayStation has paid off. The highly-anticipated Nioh 3 has gone live across both platforms, a first for a series that typically spends its initial release months as a console exclusive.

On Steam, and despite having only been available for just a few hours, the game has broken series records, and it continues to climb.

At the time of writing, Nioh 3 has peaked at 42,822 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), and the number keeps going up. Because it’s in the middle of day in Europe and everyone is at work, it’s entirely possible - if not likely - that this figure will get much higher. A weekend bump is also possible, as we’ve seen with several recent releases.

As it stands, the current peak concurrent is enough to get the game in Steam’s top 20 most played games.

It has been revealed that this already puts it ahead of all other Nioh games on Steam. The original Nioh peaked at 10,649 when it released in November, 2017. Nioh 2 fared much better, peaking at 41,325 concurrent players in February, 2021.

Sources indicate that of course, you could see that success coming a mile away. The game is presently number one worldwide in Steam’s list of top sellers. This is a jump of 46 positions, for a total of three weeks Nioh 3 has spent in that list.

Industry observers note that there are many reasons as to why Nioh 3 has done as well as it has. Word of mouth coming off last year’s PS5-exclusive demo, and the more positive coverage that followed since are just two.

Just last week, Team Ninja released a pretty generous demo across both platforms, which has been well received by players, and likely contributed to sales, in no small part because progress in the demo carries over to the full game.

Critical reviews have been incredibly positive, too. We awarded the game four out of five stars, calling it “Team Ninja’s most accomplished action game, and the series’ most accessible.” It will be interesting to see what number the highest peak concurrent actually settles on over the weekend.

Recent findings suggest that until then, if you’re jumping in yourself, our Nioh 3 guides are essential reading. Start off with these useful and actually informative gameplay tips, and don’t start playing until you’ve changed these settings. Once you’re ready to get deeper, be sure to read up on how to play co-op with other players, and how to summon AI Acolytes to help you out.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, the upcoming major release is dubbed No Aha at Full Moon for a very good reason.
  • It has been revealed that planarcadia is a place whose description sounds a bit like a Warhammer 40,000 Eldar homeworld, and is quite open about its cyberpunk inspirations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, hoYoverse just wrapped up a major Honkai: Star Rail Special Program. We’ve been waiting for this one for a couple of weeks now thanks to a delay, but the developer has finally delivered all the news on Version 4.0, which will arrive February 13.

In a recent development, the upcoming major release is dubbed No Aha at Full Moon for a very good reason. Aha's Planarcadia is the major newly introduced world headlining Version 4.0.

It has been revealed that planarcadia is a place whose description sounds a bit like a Warhammer 40,000 Eldar homeworld, and is quite open about its cyberpunk inspirations. In-universe, however, it was born out of the pages of an art canvas, and it’s a world where pleasure is king.

Industry observers note that the squad’s host in this chapter is Madam Pearl, who will oversee the the Astral Express’ return to the place where they first began their journey. Duomension City is where you’re going to land, and meet the creatures that dwell in this world.

Sources indicate that the imagenae of Planarcadia require attention to survive, and they feed off people’s Wishpower. If they don’t get any attention, they perish, which does tie into the general themes of the place. Duomension City has other interesting locations that you’re going to visit, such as the Graphia Academy art school, the commercial district of Dovebrook, and a few other places hidden behind mysterious entrances.

The Phantasmoon Games is another highlight of Planarcadia, a competitive spectacle where you’ll have a chance to compete to become Aeon for a Minute. If you make it to the final stages, you may earn an audience with The Laughter.

Much like the world where the games take place, the whole point of the competition is to attract the most attention, so rules are a bit loose as to how you manage to do that. The event will bring together several of the game’s factions, though not everyone is there for the competition.

It has been revealed that as you explore Planarcadia, if you have characters on your team who are on the newly-playable Path of Elation, you’ll earn Punchlines. The more you accumulate, the closer you get to catching Aha’s attention, which triggers Aha Instant.

Version 4.0 introduces two latest 5-Star characters to Honkai: Star Rail. General Yao Guang (Madam Yao) is one, a Seer Strategist from the Xianzhou Alliance's Yuque. If you’ve been playing the game, you may already be familiar with her voice, as she's previously been in touch with our heroes via radio link. But V4.0 marks her first on-screen appearance, as well as her playable debut.

General Yao Guang is a Physical character on the Path of Elation whose specialty is using Weal and Woe Lots in battle, which she uses to increase Elation for allies, and grant everyone Punchline any time she uses a Skill. If an Aha Instant is triggered, she casts Woe Lots, which debuff enemies, causing them to take increased damage, all while regenerating Skill Points for the rest of the team.

Industry observers note that her aptly named Certified Banger buff adds one extra instance of Elation to teammates’ attacks. And her Ultimate grants the team Punchline, and triggers an extra Aha Instant.

The other latest arrival is likewise a Path of Elation devotee. Sparxie is a suspiciously familiar streamer who uses her influencer skills in combat. When she fights, she turns the fight into a battle for attention, as she forces enemies to engage in a race for upvotes.

When you consume Skill Points, Sparxie will get gifts, which in turn cause her to regenerate Skill Points and Punchlines for the team. You can continue doing this to increase your damage. When Aha Instant is triggered, Sparxie unleashes a lucky draw that deals damage to enemies with each bounce.

She also benefits from the Certified Banger state, which causes the gifs she receives to deal more Elation damage to a random enemy target. Her Ultimate also deals more Elation damage.

Version 4.0 will see a few re-runs, too. Black Swan, Evernight, and Hysilens will be part of the first half's Warp events. The second half will see the return of Sparkle, Cerydra, and Rappa — that's right, HoYoverse have finally remembered Rappa exists, after one of the longest rerun waits in the game's history! Both Black Swan and Sparkle are getting a few tweaks to their kit with this version, too, so the timing works.

According to recent reports, finally, the other major news is a Fortnite collaboration. Starting February 26, Kafka and Blade will join Epic’s battle royale shooter. On that day, you’ll find skins of the two Stellaron Hunters in the Fortnite Item Shop, and the upcoming outfits are even compatible with Fortnite's LEGO styles. You can also expect other customisation bits like Back Bling, Pickaxe, and more to be part of the package.

If you download the game on the Epic Games Store, and take part in Honkai: Star Rail-themed activities, you’ll also get the Blade character outfit in Fortnite for free. Event schedule and timing will be unveiled at a later date.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • Getting your finances in order doesn't require a business degree or a meeting with your accountant.
  • Recent findings suggest that to get a bank account in GTA 6, you'll first need to progress through the main story until you get Lucia out of jail.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Living in Leonida isn't cheap, and being a wanted criminal doesn't mean you get to skip the boring financial stuff. If you've been trying to treat yourself to some upcoming clothes or other goodies in GTA 6, you might have run into a rather annoying little problem: some stores won't let you shop without a bank account. Rude!

Getting your finances in order doesn't require a business degree or a meeting with your accountant. You'll just need to get familiar with the game's banking system and figure out how to manage your cash. Here's everything you need to know to get your money situation sorted.

Recent findings suggest that to get a bank account in GTA 6, you'll first need to progress through the main story until you get Lucia out of jail. Shortly afterward (the day after the first night, in fact), she will call you, asking you to open a bank account.

It has been revealed that you'll then visit a bank and speak with the manager, who will explain that he can't open a traditional account for you. Instead, he'll direct you to the BuckMe application. During the cutscene, you'll automatically open the app and set up your account.

Once BuckMe is unlocked, you can deposit your cash at ATMs and use your bank balance to purchase items that require a bank account.

Recent findings suggest that to find the nearest ATM, pull out your phone by pressing up on the D-pad and open the BuckMe application. Select the ATM Locations option (by scrolling down) using the D-pad, and the closest ATM will be marked on your map.

Drive to the location and interact with the ATM to deposit the cash you're carrying into your BuckMe account. You can then use those funds to purchase items at stores that require a bank account.

BuckMe also gives you access to a Family Savings account, which you can transfer money into directly through the application. You'll need to deposit $5,000 into Family Savings to progress through a later quest, so make sure you set aside some money for it while keeping enough in your regular account for shopping.

It has been revealed that some items can still be purchased with physical cash, so you don't need to deposit everything you earn. However, getting BuckMe set up early will make shopping and managing your money much easier throughout GTA 6.

Industry News: Guide: GTA 6: Tips & Tricks You Need to Know

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1440 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pushsquare

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • GTA 6's vast open world is begging to be explored, but before you sink your teeth into Leonida, there are a handful of tips and tricks you should know.
  • Below are 12 spoiler-free GTA 6 tips and tricks that will improve your life in Leonida:.
  • GTA 6 doesn't have traditional difficulty options like other games, but there are a couple of ways you can make Leonida more manageable.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6's vast open world is begging to be explored, but before you sink your teeth into Leonida, there are a handful of tips and tricks you should know. This spoiler-free GTA 6 guide includes info on a dozen key features and mechanics that will help you make the best start to your life in Vice City.

Below are 12 spoiler-free GTA 6 tips and tricks that will improve your life in Leonida:.

GTA 6 doesn't have traditional difficulty options like other games, but there are a couple of ways you can make Leonida more manageable.

Industry observers note that press Options and select Settings > Gameplay. Scroll to the bottom (options 24 and 25) and you can choose to enable Accessible Combat and Reduced Vehicle Damage, as shown:.

Accessible Combat will both reduce the damage you take in gunfights, while increasing the damage enemies receive, making firefights much more manageable.

Reduced Vehicle Damage, meanwhile, will reduce the damage your car takes when in crashes or combat. This means there's less chance of your car becoming difficult to control or exploding.

The game will warn you that enabling these "changes the balance and experience of gameplay", meaning your experience will be a lot easier. Using them does not alter the story or disable Trophies, however.

GTA 6 has a new control scheme which modernises its gameplay by mapping run to L3 and jump to Cross/X.

For those of you who've spent over a decade playing GTA 5 and GTA Online, however, you may prefer to use Rockstar's more traditional control scheme.

Fortunately, this is relatively easy to enable.

Press Options and select Settings > Control Scheme, as pictured:.

The control scheme will automatically be set to the upcoming Default layout, but you can toggle to Classic if you prefer the GTA 5 approach.

As its name implies, GTA 6 is all about grand theft auto — or, in other words, stealing cars.

Most vehicles you find parked around Vice City will be locked, but it is possible to steal them quicker with a very simple tip.

When the minigame for any criminal activities appear — like using your Slim Jim, Clone Key, or even hotwiring a car — there's a pink "sweet spot" you can find to speed up the action:.

This makes it quicker to break in and make a quick getaway.

Just move the sticks around to find the right spot, and use those extra seconds wisely to escape swiftly:.

Industry observers note that GTA 6 has a living, breathing open world that encourages exploration. If you take the time to look around, you'll almost certainly discover something to do.

However, if you want to continue with the story and you're not sure what to do next, there's a way to easily see your next objective or story mission.

Press the Touch Pad to open your map and then using the index on the left of the screen, press Right to see a list of available story missions, with mandatory objectives at the top and optional ones listed below:.

You can immediately set a waypoint to any mission with Cross/X.

There is no traditional fast travel in GTA 6, but there is a way you can get around the map quickly for a nominal fee.

Bring up your smartphone by pressing Up and select RydeMe:.

You'll need to have an active waypoint, which you can choose from within the app or by picking one in advance via your map with Touch Pad.

You'll be notified a driver is on the way and you'll be able to see them from your minimap:.

It has been revealed that once you get in your Ryde, hold L2 to focus on your driver. You can then hold Triangle to skip your journey for $100 and immediately arrive at your destination:.

Longer journeys will cost more than shorter ones, but fast travelling this way is relatively inexpensive overall.

In a recent development, there are two types of money in GTA 6: cash stored in your wallet and money protected in your BuckMe bank. The latter will unlock as part of Chapter 1.

You can see both types of money at any time by pushing Down:.

Money stored in your wallet will be lost if you're Busted or Wasted during gameplay, so it's really important you put this in your BuckMe bank.

The easiest way to do this is press Up to access your smartphone and select BuckMe > ATM Finder:.

Sources indicate that this will automatically select a waypoint to the nearest ATM machine. Follow it and deposit any funds in your wallet into your BuckMe bank, where it'll be safe even if you get arrested or die:.

Throughout GTA 6, Jason and Lucia will build a criminal profile which can affect how NPCs and the wider world of Leonida responds to you.

Murdering enemies will contribute towards a more aggressive criminal profile. As such, you may want to consider a non-lethal approach.

One way to do this is by favouring stealth and grabbing enemies with R2, so you can cleanly knock them out without killing them:.

Another option, if you get caught up in a gunfight, is to target non-vitals like kneecaps and arms.

You can easily see non-vitals by pressing L3 and R3 and aiming at yellow parts of the body:.

You'll know an enemy has been debilitated without killing them if a yellow X appears in your weapon's reticule. A red X will appear if your target has been murdered.

If you need to set a quick waypoint to an notable location in GTA 6, you don't necessarily need to press Touch Pad to bring up your map.

Instead, hold Down and you'll get an alternative in-game view of any nearby shops, waypoints, or story missions:.

You can highlight any of these and press R3 to automatically set a GPS route to where you want to go.

There'll be times in GTA 6 when you're separated from your car and you want to spawn it nearby.

You can do this by opening your smartphone with Up and selecting the Scooter Bros app:.

Select which car you want to use from the app and you'll be charged a fee depending on the delivery distance and your car's current condition:.

Your car will then automatically spawn in a nearby location, marked on your minimap:.

Stealing or entering a car in GTA 6 does not mean you'll have access to it forever.

You'll need to park it in a Parking Space or Garage to temporarily store it, and register it at a Pay 'N' Spray to keep it forever.

Find a car you want to keep and set a waypoint for a Pay 'N' Spray, like with this Emperor Sultan I just stole:.

Drive into the Pay 'N' Spray and select Register to swap the plates. The fee commanded will depend on the value of the car:.

According to recent reports, note that you will need free Stored Vehicle slots to register your car. You can sell previous cars directly at the Pay 'N' Spray:.

Alternatively, you can press Up to open your smartphone and select Vice City Real Estate. This will let you buy more garages for additional Parking Spots:.

This feature becomes available during a story mission, so you may not immediately have access to it if you're still early in the campaign.

Generic upgrades are available for all vehicles at any Mod Shop, but if you want specialist tunings you need to go to the right shop.

These are marked with a blue Wrench icon.

Press Up to open your map and then Right to open the map index.

Select Vehicles > Mod Shops and look for a Mod Shop with a blue Wrench icon, as shown:.

Set a waypoint for the appropriate Mod Shop and you'll find all of the customisations and specialised upgrades available for your current vehicle.

Just like in real-life, staying on top of your smartphone notifications in GTA 6 can be time consuming.

Fortunately, the game will mark key messages for you in the Reminders tab:.

Press Up to bring up your smartphone and then press Square to access your Reminders.

Here you'll find a curated list of key messages, including in-game news articles and NPCs who are waiting for your replies:.

Hopefully you've learned a thing or two with this spoiler-free GTA 6 walkthrough and collectibles guide. Are there any other tips and tricks you think the world should know? Share them in the comments section below.

GTA 6: How to Find the Parrot's Secret Stash

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto 6 is chock full of side quests that point you towards bonus hits or gang hideouts.
  • While picking up Jason’s neighbor Shirley’s rum order from a nearby liquor store, you just might hear some squawking the attendant writes off as a loud TV.
  • Industry observers note that to start, you’ll want to head to the Three Sheers Liquor store, marked on your map by Shirley when you accept her request to snag her rum order.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto 6 is chock full of side quests that point you towards bonus hits or gang hideouts. All over Leonida, groups of ner’do wells are making cash and leaving it lying around, all yours for the taking if you’re quick enough on the draw and know where to look.

While picking up Jason’s neighbor Shirley’s rum order from a nearby liquor store, you just might hear some squawking the attendant writes off as a loud TV. In reality, he’s hiding a pretty penny within an exotic animal ring run out the back, and a spiteful parrot is stuck back there ready to spill the beans. Let’s go over the quickest way to find it and run it for all its worth.

Industry observers note that to start, you’ll want to head to the Three Sheers Liquor store, marked on your map by Shirley when you accept her request to snag her rum order. Located just down the road from Jason’s place, enter for a small cutscene hinting there's more going on behind closed doors.

It has been revealed that once you secure Shirley’s rum in your trunk, head down the alley to the right of the store. You’ll hear a bunch of people arguing with what sounds like a parrot, insulting the crew and blabbing about hiding cash. Continue down the alley until you spot an opening in the barbed wire cover on the wall.

It has been revealed that hop over, and the gang will start a brawl. Be careful, as stepping too far away will prompt multiple members to draw their guns. If you want to get out of this quietly and professionally, make sure you handle the group hand-to-hand; that way, no one calls the cops.

It has been revealed that once you handle all the goons, the parrot will start praising you. By interacting with it, Jason will ask about the money it mentioned, and it will start dropping hints. The vital one is the generator, alluding to the small box generator in the upper left corner of the yard, behind the liquor store.

Sources indicate that go into focus mode, and you’ll notice a small marked crevice in the side of the store, right beside the generator. Interact with it to pocket a cool $1,382, a solid early-game sum that will more than pay for running Shirley’s errands. You can also pocket a number of melee weapons from the goons, including machetes and shovels if you’re looking for a hand-to-hand option.

Industry observers note that the liquor store gang is one of many small, unaffiliated criminal groups that you can find throughout Leonida, acting as a great first taste of the kind of rewards that can be hiding right out of plain sight. Return Shirley’s rum, and you’ve had a very successful errand.

Feature: 10 Features That Surprised Me While Playing GTA 6 On Xbox Series X

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1204 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Purexbox

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By now, you've hopefully had a chance to check out our review of GTA 6 for Xbox Series X elsewhere on Pure Xbox, and it exists because Rockstar gave us multiple weeks' worth of early access to the game ahead of release.
  • It has been revealed that I was the lucky person to take on the review responsibility for the new Grand Theft Auto, and I've put basically all of my free time into it since late October.
  • In a recent development, some of these were already known prior to today, whereas others might be brand-latest information.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By now, you've hopefully had a chance to check out our review of GTA 6 for Xbox Series X elsewhere on Pure Xbox, and it exists because Rockstar gave us multiple weeks' worth of early access to the game ahead of release.

It has been revealed that I was the lucky person to take on the review responsibility for the new Grand Theft Auto, and I've put basically all of my free time into it since late October. While completing the campaign, I inevitibly came across loads of features that surprised me along the way, so I thought I'd use this opportunity to just highlight a few of them.

In a recent development, some of these were already known prior to today, whereas others might be brand-latest information. In any case, here are the specific features (avoiding story spoilers) that surprised me as I was completing GTA 6 on Xbox Series X:.

Recent findings suggest that yeah, there's finally a fuel requirement in a GTA game! It's not too invasive, so don't worry, but if you happen to drive a car around the map for an extensive amount of time, you'll be forced to find a gas station and refuel it (a very short cutscene and a press of the RT button). You can also repair your car at gas stations as well, which certainly comes in handy if you've been smashing it around at high speeds!

Sources indicate that you can still break into vehicles the old fashioned way - either stealing it mid-drive or smashing a window to gain access - but you can also use a slim-jim to break the lock, or eventually a key cloner to bypass the security entirely. Be aware of vehicles with trackers though, as if you end up going too slow, the tracker will alert the cops to your location.

It's not always enough to escape the cops and stay hidden from them for an extended period of time. If you really want to ensure you'll lose their attention, you'll want to either ditch the car or take it to a "Pay 'n' Spray" outlet, as well as change your outfit. It's possible to partially do this by throwing on some sunglasses and a hat, but the clever move is to stash one or more outfits in your car's trunk that you can switch between at a moment's notice.

While it's impossible to avoid situations in GTA 6 where you'll be engaging in all sorts of criminal activity, you can handle them in various ways. For example, a mission that requires you to take out a bunch of people can be completed by one-shotting them all, but this will raise your criminal profile. Alternatively, leaving your enemies injured but still alive will push you more towards a "Professional" profile. I haven't properly been able to compare how this affects the game yet (I really need to experiment with both sides of the extreme rather than hovering towards the middle), but Rockstar states it alters how the story, world and Jason / Lucia react to you.

I always love when games get creative with music - South of Midnight was one that really impressed me - and GTA 6 is now one of the best examples I can think of. Basically, you get highly-curated pumping tunes playing in the background during things like shootouts and getaways, while more menacing situations can feature a different vibe of soundtrack, sometimes even with lyrics. You might not quite understand the appeal until you play it, but it's actually one of my favourite new features. The use of music in certain cutscenes is awesome as well.

In a recent development, I don't know if I can verify this yet for sure, but the radio stations either appear to change their music selection based on where you are on the map, or based on how far you've progressed into the story. As I spent more time in Vice City, I started to notice a much bigger range of songs on the Flash FM channel (my favourite) including everyone from Coldplay to The Ting Tings, whereas those tunes never popped up at the start. Try it for yourself and let me know if I'm right about this!

Any GTA game worth its salt has to come with a whole bunch of minigames, and my favourite so far is the addition of minigolf. I believe there are three 18-hole courses dotted around the map in total, and they're beautifully detailed and themed, with genuinely enjoyable holes to play on. There's actual golf as well, but I have to admit I haven't had chance to check it out yet. Pool in the bars is great fun too!

According to recent reports, if you really take your time to play through GTA 6, which I highly recommend you do, you'll truly be able to appreciate just how much effort has gone into some of the seemingly smallest aspects of it. Snapmatic, which is the social media platform on your in-game phone, is constantly being updated with newly introduced statuses, photos, videos, comments and more, and you could literally just sit just browsing it for ages and enjoying the interactions. There's also a "News" app that regularly gets updated with fresh articles about what's going on in Leonida.

When you get to a certain mission in GTA 6, you'll be introduced to your first video game inside the game itself, which seems to be a very high-brow parody of modern-day indie hits. There are actually multiple games you can play, including one that's very reminiscent of Xbox title Yet Another Zombie Survivors, and these can either be accessed by turning on your TV or going up to arcade cabinets located in various stores all over the map.

In a recent development, when GTA 5 came out for Xbox 360 back in 2013, one of the big things I can recall is how slow the initial loading screens would be, especially once GTA Online got involved. We obviously haven't got an online component to GTA 6 just yet, but in terms of loading up the single-player game on Xbox Series X, it's actually a very quick process that isn't painful whatsoever. You barely even notice it!

Sources indicate that of course, these aren't the only surprising features you'll run into while playing GTA 6 - there are literally hundreds and hundreds that are waiting to be discovered. I don't want to spoil anything about the story or the details of the missions themselves though, and ultimately this is a game where surprises will continue being revealed long into the future.

For now, just go and enjoy it on your Xbox Series X or Xbox Series S (or PS5), and I urge you to take your time and really let it all soak in. One of the perils of reviewing games is that you have to grind to the finish line, and while that does still give you a great impression of the experience, I already can't wait to go back and spend 100+ hours with it this time.

Anything here sound particularly enticing to you? Let us know down in the comments section below.

  • It has been revealed that in Swarmbreaker - which launches on Steam tomorrow, and still has a demo as of writing – you have to defend your rocketship against waves of insect aggressors, who spawn at the map's far corners.
  • The results are hypnotic: coloured particles burst from each burrow and course through the map's contours, pushing movable terrain elements and eroding your structures like acid.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, it is stated that King Canute once placed his throne on the shore and commanded the sea not to get his feet wet, thus proving to his flattering courtiers that only God Almighty holds sway over the elements. "But sire!" I would have told him, if I'd been one of the aforesaid lickspittles. "Why not lay down spike strips and park a couple of flamethrowers in the shallows?" I would have said this because I have just been playing Swarmbreaker, a tower defence game that aims to prove there is no fluid body so awe-inspiring that it cannot be machine-gunned into submission.

It has been revealed that in Swarmbreaker - which launches on Steam tomorrow, and still has a demo as of writing – you have to defend your rocketship against waves of insect aggressors, who spawn at the map's far corners. Between waves, you spend earnings from kills on turrets, barricades, troops, and upgrades for all the foregoing. Sounds like bog-standard attrition management, perhaps, but what lifts Swarmbreaker is the "swarm" part. The rapacious scuttlers come in several distinct varieties, but they also "cluster, collide and flow like a fluid".

The results are hypnotic: coloured particles burst from each burrow and course through the map's contours, pushing movable terrain elements and eroding your structures like acid. You can practically hear the oil derricks fizz as they are engulfed and chewed to a lumpy puddle of iridescent digestive enzymes. Speaking of which, the more oil derricks you save during each wave, the more cash you'll have to spend before the next, but committing to their protection obviously risks leaving your ship exposed. Your fallback option is an inexhaustible mouse-click-fired artillery cannon, but this won't save you if the bulk of the swarm makes it all the way to your doorstep.

I'm still not convinced this isn't a run-of-the-mill tower defender, beneath it all, but it's worth giving the demo a shot just to enjoy the swirling tidal dynamics of homocidal buglife. What would King Canute have made of it all? I think he would have stuck his throne right by the biggest burrow, surrounded by gravity traps and howitzers. "Back in your hole, hungry liquids!" he'd have bellowed, firing dual AK47s simultaneously. "The only god I recognise is efficient chokepoint management! Death to sense-of-flow! Death to trickle-down politics!".

According to recent reports, "SIRE," I'd have told him sternly. "You are getting your metaphors confused. And also that is a total waste of howitzers - those things are best placed on hills." Read more on Steam.
